newsitem.title: USA: U.S. study finds risk of morning fainting spells.
newsitem.headline: U.S. study finds risk of morning fainting spells.

text.p: A study of long-term nursing home residents found that about half suffered rapid changes in blood pressure that led to fainting spells and falls, especially before breakfast, researchers said Tuesday.

The study from the Hebrew Rehabilitation Center for Aged in Boston, suggests that "attention probably should be directed toward the early morning period before breakfast when elderly people arise from bed to prevent...falls."
The research involved 911 patients aged 60 and beyond.

The phenomenon may be linked to the time of day that certain blood pressure medications are administered, usually beginning with breakfast, said the study published in this week's Journal of the American Medical Association.
